StreamingChatCompletions at lines 443-481 implements a separate synchronous iterator and explicit response lifecycle around the shared parser; EOF closes but a parsed DONE marker itself does not call close. This behavior is supported directly by the bounded source.

AsyncStreamingChatCompletions at lines 484-523 implements the corresponding async byte iterator, queued-update yield and awaited close paths. The proposal correctly limits the close claim to EOF, context exit and explicit aclose rather than a parsed DONE marker.

limitations: These are analyst proposals awaiting independent AI review, not human-verified findings. Both supplied files are populated customization patches with substantive bodies, but downstream generated behavior and complete public activation are not independently established.

Coverage is partial: two fragments/two paths among 37 eligible and 116 discovered files. The aio patch stops at 470 inside an overloaded complete declaration; its callable implementation is not supplied. The models patch stops at 574 inside patch_sdk's docstring. Three skipped-path entries include these truncations and the prompts patch.

The async complete overloads and their documentation do not establish a completion request body, error mapping, default-setting application or streaming dispatch implementation. Imported request builders, error classes and _get_internal_response_format are not counted as implemented behavior.

ChatCompletionsClient.__init__ also stores default settings and calls the internal response-format helper, but these behaviors share the exact proposed constructor path/symbol identity. They are not split with synthetic aliases, and the absent complete implementation does not prove those stored defaults are used as described by comments.

The constructor comment says generated code sets Authorization while this patch adds api-key. Only the latter mutation and superclass call are supplied; no actual dual-header transmission, credential rotation or case-normalization behavior is asserted.

The model patch exports the proposed public message/model/iterator names. Base-model constructors, rest_field/rest_discriminator implementation, model deserializer and full public client wiring are not supplied, so role forwarding and field declarations are not treated as independently verified wire serialization or validation.

The SSE parser uses prefix tests rather than exact DONE equality, skips only b'\n', and returns early on incomplete tails. It does not itself set _done or close the response; supplied iterator callers assign its return value. No full SSE conformance, automatic close on all failures, valid arbitrary chunk stream or successful runtime parsing was tested.

The frozen module identity remains python:azure-ai-inference:module-v1. Library latestRelease is 1.0.0b9 and stable is false; no package-version source is supplied. The specification commit is separate generation context, not the SDK commit or evidence of a completed generator run.

No SDK code, local media file loading, model endpoint, paid model call or external URL was executed. No root cause, recurrence or reducibility was measured; generator-addressable means plausible code-generation support in principle.

The evidence covers only aio/_patch.py lines 1-470 and models/_patch.py lines 1-574 of 37 eligible files among 116 discovered files. Both excerpts stop mid-file; prompts/_patch.py and other eligible code are not supplied, so this is not an absence finding for the remaining library.

The aio excerpt contains ChatCompletionsClient.complete overload declarations but stops before the final overload documentation/body; streaming, request serialization, default-parameter application and any other operational behavior of complete cannot be adjudicated from signatures or docstrings alone.

ChatCompletionsClient.__init__ also stores request-setting defaults and transforms response_format at lines 224-261. This is additional behavior on the same declaration/path identity as the reviewed constructor-header finding, not a distinct-key omission; without the complete body, the claimed later application of defaults and behavior of _get_internal_response_format are unverified.

The model excerpt stops within the patch_sdk docstring at line 574; its actual body, if any, is unavailable. Message-model superclass behavior, generated client internals and final export/activation wiring outside these two patches are not supplied. Nonempty models __all__ at lines 553-567 is a handwritten signal, not proof that every declared runtime export is activated.

The target remains python:azure-ai-inference:module-v1 as frozen even though the library metadata names a beta release. generatorAddressable=yes means plausible generic TypeSpec/generator support, not measured recurrence across services, active-library status or proven reducibility. Accepted and revised decisions are AI-reviewed, not human-verified; human overrides remain authoritative.
